lines.text: Today you become a shopping detective. You will find the real best deal, spot ad tricks, and check every bill.
The same thing can cost different amounts in different shops or apps.
Before you buy, check at least two places.
A few minutes of checking can save real money.
Unit price means the price of one piece, or one kilo.
Two pens for ₹20 is ₹10 a pen, but three pens for ₹27 is ₹9 a pen.
The bigger pack is cheaper for each pen, but only if you need all three.
Buy one get one free sounds great, but it only saves money if you really need two.
Half price means you pay only half of the normal price.
Ask yourself: would I buy this if there was no offer?
Ads are made to make you want things.
They use famous faces, bright colours, catchy songs and words like ‘Hurry, last day!’.
Enjoy the ad, then ask what the product really does.
Always check the bill before you pay, and count your change after.
Make sure each item and price is right and nothing is added twice.
Shopkeepers are busy, and mistakes happen.
A small biscuit pack costs ten rupees, and a family box of four packs costs thirty six rupees.
Thirty six divided by four is nine, so each pack in the box costs nine rupees.
The family box is cheaper for each pack, but only if your family will eat all four.
A deal is only smart when the price is better and you really need the amount.
Aarav needs one drawing book for a school project, and it costs forty rupees.
Another shop shouts buy one get one free, but the pair costs seventy rupees.
Aarav needs only one book, so the offer would cost him thirty rupees more.
A free item is not a saving if you did not need it in the first place.
Zoya buys pencils for twenty rupees, an eraser for five rupees and a notebook for forty rupees.
She adds it up herself and gets sixty five rupees, but the bill says seventy five.
She politely shows the shopkeeper, who thanks her and fixes the bill.
Zoya pays with a hundred rupee note and counts her change, thirty five rupees.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
